what: Can the reader's own confidence replace or improve the reranker-score refusal gate and the passage choice? Offline grid over scripts/tune_reader_signals.py on reports/reader_signals.json (220 answerable + 30 out-of-base questions; top-3 reranked passages, span + score + 'null wins' flag from the span reader for each).
grid: 192 combinations (passage choice x rerank threshold {none,0,1,2} x reader-score threshold {0..0.5} x use no-answer flag), constraint F1 >= baseline - 0.01
result: Only the rerank-score threshold appears among the configurations that stay within the F1 budget (t1=1: 13/30 refused for -0.008 raw F1; t1=0: 10/30). No combination with a reader-score threshold or the no-answer flag does better. Half-split check: chosen on even questions, evaluated on odd ones, 5/14 strict out-of-base refused with 7/110 false refusals.
conclusion: Reader confidence is informative but weaker than, and redundant with, the reranker score; keep the reranker-score gate (tau_r = 1.0).
caveat: Raw span F1 here is not the spoken-sentence F1 of the end-to-end table; the 30 out-of-base questions include four that Wikipedia can answer, so 'strict' counts use 26.
